chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who engraves upon his ring the Name of Allah, let him withdraw it from the hand with which he cleans himself during the ablution.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing a ring with Allah's name while performing istinja?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from Imam Ali (AS), highlights the principle of *ikram al-ism al-sharif* (honoring the Divine Name) by preventing its contact with impurities during *istinja'*. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the physical reverence due to Allah's name, distinguishing between mere presence and direct contact with *najis* (impurity), thereby guiding believers in maintaining ritual dignity in daily acts of purification.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who engraves upon his ring the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so let him withdraw it from the hand with which he cleans himself during the ablution’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘If one engraves the name of Allah on his ring he must change it from the hand with which one performs cleansing (washing one’s bottom).”’
